clue.text: Bill's companion receives medal with a Marine unit

indicators.note: the companion word takes the following pieces into its middle, as a host receives guests

parts.note: the phrase 'bill and coo' pairs the two words, so coo keeps bill company
MM is the Military Medal
with and and both join things together

explanation.surface: A man named Bill and his friend get a decoration in the Royal Marines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name, but it comes from the lovers' phrase 'bill and coo', where the dove's call keeps the bill company.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier of an amphibious raiding force, and the Royal Marines' units are commandos.

clue.text: Possible alto taken in by with-it singer

indicators.note: the reworked letters are enclosed by the piece that follows, as a guest is taken in

parts.note: C stands for Latin cum, meaning with, and IT is as written

indicators.note: a possible version of the word is one of its potential rearrangements

explanation.surface: A trendy vocalist might sing alto, the clue suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possible' rearranges the voice-part word, and 'taken in by' sets it between the two pieces of 'with-it'; C for with is the Latin cum. The bird is a small British tit.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird is a songbird, and crosswords often call any songbird a singer.

clue.text: Serviceman consuming fish spread

indicators.note: the first word eats the second, so the fish ends up inside the serviceman

parts.note: a marine is a member of a naval fighting service
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A sailor-soldier eats fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spread' looks like a verb going with the fish, but it is the noun for something put on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Margarine is a butter substitute that people put on bread.

clue.text: Grow together in a cold island

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps
Crete is the large Greek island

explanation.surface: Two things fuse while sitting on a chilly island.
explanation.definitionFit: To accrete is to build up by things fusing or gathering, as layers of sediment do.

clue.text: Is suspended for beginning to dispute points of view

indicators.note: the beginning of the following word is its opening letter only

parts.note: angles are standpoints or slants on a subject

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from opening an argument because of their various perspectives.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that dangles hangs loosely from a point above it.

clue.text: He espouses religious abstinence comparatively quickly

explanation.surface: A pious man who goes without food also moves more quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: One who fasts for his faith is one who abstains, and the comparative of the adverb fast also means more quickly.

clue.text: Looking ahead on behalf of son in crew

parts.note: acting for someone is acting on their behalf

indicators.note: the son's letter goes within the rowing crew

parts.note: an eight is a rowing boat's crew of eight oarsmen
S is the abbreviation for son in genealogies

explanation.surface: Planning ahead for the sake of a boy who rows in a team.
explanation.walkthrough: S goes inside EIGHT, after its E. An eight is the crew of a racing rowing boat, as in the Oxford and Cambridge Boat Race.
explanation.definitionFit: Foresight is the habit of anticipating what the future needs.

clue.text: Thus a small number embrace a system for electing a singer

indicators.note: the outer pieces hug the voting system between them

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
No. is the abbreviation for number
PR is proportional representation, an electoral system

explanation.surface: A tiny group of voters adopt a voting method to choose a vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Embrace' puts the electoral system between 'thus' and 'a small number'; 'a singer' looks like the object of electing but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is a singer with the highest female or boy's voice.

clue.text: Draconian instruction for soldiers to go off without one

indicators.note: the word for leaving is to lose the numeral one

parts.note: exit means leave, go off the stage
I is the Roman numeral one
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: A harsh order tells troops to leave, minus one of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a stage direction, 'Exit REME', an instruction for soldiers to go off. EXIT loses I to give EXT.
explanation.definitionFit: Draconian measures are harsh in the utmost degree, named after the severe Athenian lawgiver Draco.

clue.text: Car a friend crashed into a humpbacked cow

indicators.note: a car that has crashed is wrecked, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: A friend drives a car into a cow with a hump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crashed into' reads as one action, but 'crashed' rearranges CAR A FRIEND and 'into' just leads to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Africander is a South African breed of cattle with a hump on its shoulders.

clue.text: Father loses right to be head

indicators.note: the word for father drops the letter for right

parts.note: pater is Latin for father, used in old British schoolboy slang

explanation.surface: A dad gives up his rights in order to lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Pate is an old word for the top of the head.

clue.text: Implausible description of Stevenson's donkey-work?

parts.note: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Travels with a Donkey in the Cevennes, so his account is a travel story, and a far-fetched yarn has the same name

explanation.walkthrough: 'Donkey-work' looks like drudgery, but it points to Stevenson's book about walking with a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a tall story, the kind of exaggerated account returning voyagers were said to tell.

clue.text: It enables us to reach instant additional information

parts.note: a trice is a moment, as in 'in a trice'
PS, postscript, is information added at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Something lets us get hold of extra details straight away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reach' seems to mean getting at information, but it is stretching out an arm.
explanation.definitionFit: The muscle at the back of the upper arm straightens the elbow, so it extends the arm outward.

clue.text: Worth a king's ransom? That's hilarious!

explanation.surface: Something is enormously valuable, or else very funny.
explanation.definitionFit: Something beyond price is invaluable, and in slang a very funny thing is also beyond price.

clue.text: Took no notice of soldiers involved in wrongdoing

indicators.note: doing something wrong garbles it, so these letters get mixed together

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: Someone overlooked troops taking part in misbehaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrongdoing' looks like one word meaning misconduct, but it splits: 'wrong' is the anagram signal for the word after it, with the Royal Engineers involved.
explanation.definitionFit: To ignore someone is to disregard them deliberately.

clue.text: Sort of gunner apt for offensive

indicators.note: a sort of version of these words is a loose rearrangement of their letters

explanation.surface: A suitable artilleryman for an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offensive' looks like a military attack, fitting the gunner, but it means disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repugnant is distasteful and revolting.

clue.text: Doubter thus accepted, apart from abandoning former spouse

indicators.note: the word for thus takes in the next piece, as one accepts a guest

parts.note: sic is Latin for thus, used to flag a quoted error

indicators.note: the word for apart from leaves behind the former partner

parts.note: except means apart from
an ex is a former husband or wife

explanation.surface: A skeptic is welcomed, except that they leave their ex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abandoning' takes the ex out of the word for 'apart from', and 'accepted' puts what remains inside the Latin word for thus. Sic is the note editors put after a quoted error.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptic is someone who questions accepted beliefs.

clue.text: Call most of stem cut glass

parts.note: to cry is to call out

indicators.note: the word for stem loses its final letter, leaving most of it

parts.note: a stalk is a plant stem

explanation.surface: Someone shouts that a glass stem has been snapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Crystal is fine, clear glass, often cut into decorative facets.

clue.text: Fruit takes time to get down

parts.note: a plum is a stone fruit
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit takes ages to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Get down' suggests swallowing; 'down' alone is the soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Down is the soft fluffy layer of a bird's feathers.

clue.text: 23 initially lost key to the tower

parts.note: the answer to 23 across means extravagant, and steep means overpriced

indicators.note: the initial letter of the following word is all that is taken

parts.note: E is a musical key

explanation.surface: Someone loses the key to the tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 23 across is EXORBITANT; its synonym STEEP starts this answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A steeple is a church tower topped with a spire.

clue.text: Euphorbia round the lake making an ostentatious display

indicators.note: the plant name goes round the letter for lake

parts.note: spurge is the common name for plants of the genus Euphorbia
L is the abbreviation for lake on maps

explanation.surface: A bushy plant ringing the lake makes a showy spectacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Euphorbia' is the botanical name; the common name is what the clue wants.
explanation.definitionFit: A splurge is a lavish burst of spending or show.

clue.text: Point to awkward limits of a meritocratic system

parts.note: E, east, is a compass point

indicators.note: awkward letters are ungainly and out of place, so they get rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone highlights the clumsy boundaries of a system based on merit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awkward' rearranges LIMITS into LITISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Elitism favours rule or advancement by a select, supposedly superior few.

clue.text: Bully loses head about the French voter

indicators.note: the shortened word goes about the French article
the word for bully drops its first letter, its head

parts.note: to hector is to bully or intimidate
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bully loses his leader concerning a voter from France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loses head' drops the first letter of the word for bully, and 'about' wraps the shortened word round the French article.
explanation.definitionFit: An elector is someone entitled to vote.

clue.text: Compiler is instructed by solver? I'll say!

explanation.surface: The setter is told what to do by the solver, and agrees wholeheartedly.
explanation.definitionFit: The first reading has the solver telling the compiler something; the second is a colloquial exclamation of emphatic agreement.

clue.text: It's taken in by visitors to an ancient colonnade

indicators.note: the letters are held inside these words, as a guest is taken in

explanation.surface: Tourists are fooled by an old row of columns.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in visitorS TO An.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoa was a covered walkway lined with columns in ancient Greece.

clue.text: Extravagant former social worker is without a cycle

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so these pieces surround the cycle

parts.note: ex means former
an ant is a worker in a social insect colony
an orbit is one cycle round a planet or star

explanation.surface: A lavish ex social worker has no bike.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Social worker' suggests a welfare officer, but it is an insect from a colony; 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Exorbitant prices are excessive, far beyond what is reasonable.

clue.text: Sounds like people vigorously using pincers

indicators.note: the clue says these letters match in sound the word for people using things

parts.note: plyers are people who ply, using a tool vigorously

explanation.surface: Something resembles workers busily wielding tools for gripping.
explanation.definitionFit: Pliers are pincers with jaws for gripping and bending.

clue.text: Animal driver finds old coin outside a mine entrance

indicators.note: the coin goes outside the following letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a tester was an old English sixpence

indicators.note: the entrance of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A drover finds an old coin outside the mouth of a mine.
explanation.walkthrough: A tester was a Tudor coin, later a slang name for sixpence; 'entrance' takes just the first letter of 'mine'.
explanation.definitionFit: A teamster drives a team of animals, such as oxen or horses.
